text:
Predicates:
ScheduleMeeting(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
Appear(x, y) ::: x appears in y.
HaveLunch(x, y) ::: x has lunch in y.
WorkRemotely(x, y) ::: x works remotely from y.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
InCountry(x, y) ::: x is in country y.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (ScheduleMeeting(x, y) → Appear(x, company)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x (HaveLunch(x, company) → ScheduleMeeting(x, customers)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (¬HaveLunch(x, company) → WorkRemotely(x, home)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (InCountry(x, country) → WorkRemotely(x, home)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
∀x (Manager(x) → ¬WorkRemotely(x, home)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
(Manager(james) ∧ Appear(james, company)) ⊕ ¬(Manager(james) ∨ Appear(james, company)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.
Conclusion:
HaveLunch(james, company) ::: James has lunch in the company.
